# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue with his heart, requiring regular check-ups to monitor its condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky about what he eats and food textures can be a real challenge for him.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, affecting his muscle tone and overall physical strength.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is sensitive to loud noises and gets frustrated easily in crowded or loud spaces.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, or poor vision, which requires corrective measures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs careful brushing and regular dental check-ups to prevent tooth decay and maintain oral health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced delays in reaching certain developmental milestones and requires additional support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children staying in mainstream education and obtaining qualifications, while others may need more support and some benefit from a specialist setting.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is behind his peers in terms of overall development and has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone and strength.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and has hip dysplasia, which affects his posture and movement.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A study of 40 European patients showed that 15/40 (38%) had heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and palatal reviews.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring heart condition, treating tethered cord, managing hypotonia, addressing feeding difficulties, and ensuring proper nutrition.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires out quicker than her peers, particularly during physical activities, which has been noticed since she started school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences discomfort in loud noises, suggesting a potential connection between her environment and her comfort level.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced blurry vision, which may impact her schoolwork.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and squint (strabismus).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs more frequent dental check-ups due to various issues, including cavities and sensitivity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns are common in KBG syndrome, with weak enamel being frequently seen and careful brushing essential.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires out quicker than her peers, particularly during physical activities, which impacts her ability to participate fully in lessons.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some individuals with KBG syndrome may need additional support and some benefit from specialized settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires out quicker than her peers, particularly during physical activities, which impacts her ability to participate fully in lessons.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, people with KBG syndrome typically have delays in reaching milestones such as rolling, sitting, walking, playing with toys, using cutlery, using zips and buttons, and toilet training.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and she has short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A study showed that 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, periodic hearing reviews, and palatal reviews.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with one of the heart valves that requires regular monitoring to ensure proper development and address any necessary interventions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences food textures as a bit of an issue, being very particular about what she eats and can be quite fussy if the texture isn't right. Mealtime has required patience and creativity to find foods she's comfortable with.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient developed slower than expected in reaching certain milestones like walking or sitting, and physical therapy has helped support her progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss and require treatment.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has mentioned blurry vision, particularly with distant objects, which has led to adaptations in meal times to ensure comfort and safety.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism (the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision), and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had difficulty chewing, particularly with harder foods like nuts or raw vegetables, and needs to be adapted to ensure she can eat comfortably and safely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties have been reported in many babies with KBG syndrome, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has taken longer than expected to reach certain milestones and has needed support in physical therapy to aid her progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education-wise, those with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though some may require more support and some benefit from specialist settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developed slower than expected in reaching milestones and has required support in physical therapy to aid her progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, those with KBG syndrome typically have delays, but there is a wide range of eventual ability, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and has short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A small number of children with KBG syndrome have had hip dysplasia, in which the hip joints are easily dislocated.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart valve conditions, consideration for palatal abnormalities, assessment for tethered cord, evaluation for undescended testes, consideration for skeletal assessments, review and intervention for palatal abnormalities, consideration for neurodevelopmental therapy, monitoring of posture and ensuring adequate nutrition.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced slow weight gain compared to other kids her age, and has been advised to eat nutrient-rich foods and take supplements to support her growth.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures from time to time, which are managed with medication adjustments under the guidance of her neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can be difficult to treat and may require various interventions.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media, an infection of the middle ear, which was treated with antibiotics and has since recovered.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasal grommet insertion to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means she has trouble seeing things that are far away, and corrective lenses have helped improve her vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, which may impact their daily life.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires careful and consistent dental care to prevent tooth decay and maintain oral health.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including speech delay and movement coordination issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may also have undescended testes, palatal abnormalities, and other physical differences that impact their overall development and daily life.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine, and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness and gets out of breath more quickly than other children her age, even with simple games.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more quickly than other children her age and experiences shortness of breath, especially during simple activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has bowel problems, with some foods making it worse, and requires dietary adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and subtle anomalies of the palate can affect feeding and speech development in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epileptic episodes managed with medication and lifestyle changes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to turn the volume of the TV very high, suggesting possible hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media or glue ear can cause conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction, which may impact her vision and alignment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and frequent cavities, requiring close attention to dental health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular visits to the dentist are essential to prevent complications.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs additional support in school, with some children requiring EHCP and others benefiting from mainstream education with adaptations.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and has speech delay, as well as palatal abnormalities and undescended testes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as "typical" children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to scoliosis, and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A study showed that 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic examinations to monitor growth velocity and identify potential hormonal imbalances.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Management of epilepsy with medication and lifestyle modifications, monitoring for tethered cord based on clinical findings, addressing palatal abnormalities through appropriate interventions, and ensuring adequate nutrition and physical activity to support overall health and development.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart abnormality that requires regular monitoring and management by a specialist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges with feeding, being particular about food and sometimes reluctant to try new foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, and is under the care of a neurologist to adjust treatment as necessary.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had issues with conductive hearing loss, including otitis media and glue ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as myopia (farsightedness), hypermetropia (near-sightedness), and astigmatism.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist frequently due to various tooth issues, requiring regular monitoring and treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been described as needing extra help in school, with some children requiring support in mainstream settings and others benefiting from specialized settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been noted as having behavioral differences, including potential ASD, ADHD, or anxiety.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit variability in cognitive abilities, social skills, and overall development compared to "typical" individuals.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, in which the hip joints are easily dislocated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome have subtler anomalies of the skull, spine, or hips, which may affect posture, movement, and functional ability.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, and periodic review of heart conditions.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring and managing heart conditions, treating hormonal imbalances, addressing neurological concerns, correcting palatal abnormalities, and managing feeding aversions.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing when engaging in physical activities, such as running or playing outside.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets much faster than expected when physically active, requiring monitoring of heart health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems, including bowel movements and constipation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy, which requires close monitoring and management by a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can be treated with various medications.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences otitis media, a buildup of fluid in the ear, which was previously treated with antibiotics.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as myopia, hypermetropia, and squint (strabismus).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and frequent visits to the dentist for potential issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and need for frequent dental check-ups are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient benefits from additional support in school and may require accommodations to assist with learning challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some achieving mainstream qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which may impact their development and interactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may also display characteristics similar to those with ASD, ADHD, or anxiety, but the extent varies.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may experience skeletal anomalies such as hip dysplasia, tethered cord, or asymmetric hip creases, which can affect movement and posture.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic cardiac evaluations are recommended.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring and managing heart conditions, treating epillexia, managing hormonal imbalances, addressing gastrointestinal issues, correcting palatal abnormalities, and considering orthopedic interventions as needed.
